note: Shared by assets/js/urban_dictionary.test.mjs and test/devils_dictionary/sources/urban_dictionary_slug_test.exs. Both assert that their own slug rule maps every `from` to its `to`, so the JS that builds a /define/<slug> link and the Elixir that mints the slug can never drift apart unnoticed. Measured against DevilsDictionary.Registry.Lexeme.slug/1 on 2026-09-21. The range is what an Urban Dictionary [bracket] actually holds: ASCII, Latin-1 accents, apostrophes, punctuation and the common Latin ligatures. A codepoint outside it (CJK, Cyrillic) is transliterated by the Elixir `slugify` package's data table and is not reproduced in JS; such a link lands on the miss page, which shows suggestions, rather than on a wrong word.
